description.value: A remote wilderness camp within Carmanah Walbran Park, set beneath old-growth Sitka spruce reaching 95 metres and ancient cedars over 1,000 years old; access is via active private logging roads shared with industrial trucks, making this one of the most demanding reaches on Vancouver Island.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website is BC Parks' official page for Carmanah Walbran Provincial Park, confirming Three Sisters Camp is an active provincial park campsite (fee=yes per OSM). The site provides general park information but no campsite-specific amenity details, so most amenities remain null. The park is described as extremely remote, accessed only via rough private logging roads shared with industrial logging trucks, which is a significant concern for touring cyclists.
concerns: Access to the park is via private logging roads described as narrow, bumpy, and frequented by industrial logging trucks with right-of-way; cycling access would be extremely challenging and potentially dangerous.
Website is the general BC Parks park page and provides no amenity detail specific to Three Sisters Camp itself.
No address, phone number, or email in OSM record.
Park is described as very remote with the closest emergency telephone at the Didtidaht Reserve.
OSM tag internet_access=no corroborated by website noting most parks lack internet connectivity; no device charging infrastructure expected.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: This is a legitimate active provincial park campsite but access is solely via rough, narrow private logging roads shared with industrial logging trucks — conditions that are hazardous and likely impractical for touring cyclists. The website provides no campsite-level amenity detail, and no cycling-specific infrastructure is evident.
enrichment_extras.notes: Three Sisters Camp is one of multiple unnamed or lightly documented campsites within Carmanah Walbran Provincial Park. The BC Parks general contact is 1-800-689-9025 and parkinfo@gov.bc.ca per the website contact page, but these are not campsite-specific and have not been added to the record.
